answer.justification: Hoarseness after thyroidectomy most likely reflects unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury: the nerve lies adjacent to the inferior thyroid artery/lower pole and controls intrinsic laryngeal muscles, causing vocal fold paresis. Internal laryngeal injury causes anesthesia/aspiration, external laryngeal injury weakens pitch, and edema is an early problem.

decision.reason: Standard thyroid surgery anatomy question; PubMed unlikely to add value beyond established relationships of recurrent laryngeal nerve to inferior thyroid artery and hoarseness.
